AUST0015.description: This unit supports you in developing your understanding of the Indigenous voice as an Indigenous Scholar, in fieldwork and scholarly work. You will be exploring and interacting with Aboriginal Histories and Knowledges and reflecting critically on competing narratives of knowing, being and doing. We will assess you on your participation to the unit and on your reflective and writing ability.
AUST0015.outcomes: Students are able to (1) critically evaluate histories and narratives by drawing upon Indigenous knowledge and histories; (2) locate and articulate your specific story of Indigenous knowledge; (3) critically assess academic literature associated with Indigenous agendas; and (4) work with others in classwork and fieldwork in a respectful, scholarly and collegial manner.
AUST0015.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) engagement & participation; (2) critical reflections; and (3) article reviews. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Student may be offered supplementary assessment in this unit if they meet the eligibility criteria.

AUST0063.description: Foundations of University Study builds upon your existing study and learning skills to equip you with the scholarly skills and approaches that are essential for success in a UWA degree course. We work intensively on becoming active and analytical learners, proficient in research, critical, collaborative and communication skills. This unit also has an emphasis on digital literacy and development of confidence in using a range of digital tools.
AUST0063.outcomes: Students are able to (1) show respect for cultural diversity within Indigenous Australia and beyond; (2) apply techniques to enhance self-motivation, manage learning tasks and teamwork skills within an academic environment to support independent and collaborative learning tasks; (3) use technology to research, access resources and communicate effectively to support learning; (4) analyse, paraphrase, summarise and synthesise ideas from the literature and scientific research to support effective academic writing and presentations; (5) communicate effectively with consideration of audience and purpose of task; (6) apply learning in the academic setting to real life situations; (7) critically and reflectively consider all facets of an academic career; and (8) explain the importance of academic integrity and demonstrate appropriate use of academic referencing conventions.
AUST0063.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) participation & class presentation; (2) needs analysis action plan & study skills portfolio; and (3) research essay. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Student may be offered supplementary assessment in this unit if they meet the eligibility criteria.

AUST0075.description:
This creative writing unit has been designed to investigate the universal significance of story. Through the exploration of weekly topics, you will: prepare for lectures and tutorial workshops; engage in active learning tasks to encourage critical and analytical thought; take part in discussion on a variety of literary works and forms, including memoir.

You will also: write and revise own creative works; learn how to edit, demonstrating ethical and cultural responsibility in writing practice; research and expose current thinking on identity, voice and lived experience, understanding the importance of academic integrity; and discover insights in reflections of self, peer, and tutor evaluations.
AUST0075.outcomes: Students are able to (1) use creative writing as a form of enquiry-based learning and research; (2) apply literary techniques with ethical and cultural considerations; (3) apply critical understanding through reading texts and in the exploration of creative writing; (4) craft, revise and edit longer creative pieces; (5) demonstrate critical reading skills; and (6) explain how creative concepts and creative writing are forms of cultural practice.
AUST0075.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) participation & online journal; (2) text analysis & response; and (3) creative writing piece & commentary. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Student may be offered supplementary assessment in this unit if they meet the eligibility criteria.
